available liquidity sources are adequate to meet our credit commitments and contractual obligations over the next twelve months. </span></div><div id="iee38af5ba60d4130b71322a4e0c83ec1_220"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Item 3. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk</span></div><div id="iee38af5ba60d4130b71322a4e0c83ec1_223"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Market Risk</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Market risk represents the potential for loss resulting from adverse changes in the market value or pricing of financial instruments. Our market risk primarily arises from interest rate risk inherent in our lending, investment, deposit-taking, and funding activities. To address this significant component of market risk, management actively monitors and manages interest rate exposure.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our profitability is sensitive to fluctuations in interest rates. A sudden and material change in interest rates across different points on the yield curve may adversely affect earnings if the rates applicable to assets and liabilities do not adjust at the same pace, magnitude, or on comparable terms. We monitor the impact of interest rate changes on net interest income with the primary objective of minimizing adverse effects on net interest income and capital, while structuring our asset-liability mix to optimize the yield-cost spread. The Asset/Liability Committee (&#8220;ALCO&#8221;) of the Board of Directors meets at least quarterly to review interest rate risk and related strategies.</span></div><div id="iee38af5ba60d4130b71322a4e0c83ec1_226"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Interest Rate Sensitivity</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Interest rate risk represents the potential impact on earnings and asset values from changes in market interest rates. This risk arises primarily from timing differences in the repricing of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, embedded options such as loan prepayments, and shifts in the yield curve.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We manage interest rate risk through ALCO. Strategies include adjusting the mix and repricing characteristics of the loan and investment portfolios as well as managing the rate and maturity structure of deposit products offered and wholesale funding sources utilized.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Management employs tools such as net interest margin projection reports and interest rate simulations under various scenarios to monitor exposure and ensure compliance with ALCO limits. The simulation model is based on the maturity and repricing characteristics of our interest rate sensitive assets and liabilities. The model also incorporates various assumptions, which management believes to be reasonable but may have a significant impact on the results. What can deviate from the modeled scenarios include the timing and magnitude of changes in interest rates, the yield curve evolution and shape, the correlation between various interest rate indices, financial instruments&#8217; spread relative to benchmark rates. The modeled results are highly sensitive to deposit mix and deposit beta assumptions, which are derived from a regression analysis of our historical deposit data.</span></div><div style="height:45pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="padding-left:9pt;padding-right:9pt;text-align:center;text-indent:-18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">60</span></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"/><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><span><br/></span></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">While actual outcomes cannot be predicted with certainty, these models help assess potential impacts on net interest income and capital. If potential changes to the net equity value and net interest income resulting from hypothetical interest rate changes are not within the limits established by ALCO, we may adjust the asset and liability mix to bring the risk position within the limits or take other remediation actions.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The following table presents the estimated effect of instantaneous parallel shifts of interest rate yield curve on our projected net interest income over the next 12 months, assuming no balance sheet growth, as of the dates indicated. The scenarios presented are hypothetical and are not indicative of expected interest rate movements.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify"><table style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As of September&#160;30, 2026, model simulations indicate that projected net interest income over the next 12 months is less sensitive to declining interest rate scenarios when changes in interest rates are less than 300 basis points, compared to as of December&#160;31, 2025. This change was primarily driven by a reduction in rate-sensitive cash and cash equivalents as a percentage of earning assets at September&#160;30, 2026, compared to December&#160;31, 2025, and an increase in commercial real estate loans. While yields on cash and cash equivalents adjust immediately with changes in market interest rates, our commercial real estate loans generally have an initial five-year fixed-rate period. In addition, interest-bearing deposits comprised a larger share of total deposits as of September&#160;30, 2026, compared to December&#160;31, 2025, increasing the extent to which deposit costs decline when interest rates fall. However, this moderation in sensitivity to decreasing rates in the September 30, 2026 simulation as compared to December 31, 2025 does not extend to the most severe declining-rate scenario. The greater sensitivity in net interest income when interest rates decline 300 basis points at September 30, 2026 compared with December 31, 2025 reflects greater potential downward repricing of certain variable-rate loans. As these loans repriced upward during 2026 when the market interest rates increased, their current rates moved further above their contractual interest rate floors, providing more capacity for rates to decline before reaching those floors at September 30, 2026 than at December 31, 2025.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our model simulation results show an asymmetrical change in net interest income in rising interest rate scenarios compared to falling interest rate scenarios for all periods presented. This asymmetry is primarily driven by higher assumed deposit betas on interest-bearing deposits in rising rate environments. In rising market rate scenarios, we modeled greater pass-through of market rate increases to our interest-bearing deposit accounts, hence reducing the projected interest income benefit. Conversely, in declining interest rate scenarios, we modeled lower deposit repricing betas, as management believes that it would be more difficult to pass through market rate decreases to interest-bearing deposit accounts, especially for those accounts bearing below-market interest rates. These assumptions reflect management&#8217;s judgment based on historical experience, competitive conditions, and current market dynamics and may differ from actual deposit repricing behavior.</span></div><div id="iee38af5ba60d4130b71322a4e0c83ec1_229"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Item 4. Controls and Procedures</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</span></div><div style="text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our management, with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of the design and operation of our disclosure controls and procedures, as defined in Rule 13a-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;), as of September&#160;30, 2026. Based on this evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of the end of the fiscal quarter covered by this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q. </span></div><div style="text-align:justify"><span><br/></span></div><div style="height:45pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="padding-left:9pt;padding-right:9pt;text-align:center;text-indent:-18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">61</span></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"/><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><span><br/></span></div></div><div style="text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Changes in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</span></div><div style="text-align:justify"><span><br/></span></div><div style="text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">There have been no changes in the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rule 13a-15(f) under the Exchange Act) during the quarter ended September&#160;30, 2026 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting.</span></div><div id="iee38af5ba60d4130b71322a4e0c83ec1_232"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Part II - Other Information</span></div><div id="iee38af5ba60d4130b71322a4e0c83ec1_235"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Item 1. We have been and may in the future be involved in legal proceedings, litigation, claims and investigations in the ordinary course of business. In addition, the nature of our business exposes us to claims related to, among others, lending and deposit activities, employment practices, contractual obligations and business operations.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">There are no pending, or to management&#8217;s knowledge, any threatened legal proceedings that management believes to be material to our business, financial condition, or results of operations.
